_comment_regions: PIN THE FUNCTIONS WHERE THE DATABASE IS.
This was unset, which means Vercel used the account default — normally
iad1, US East. The Supabase project resolves to an AWS EU address range
(2a05:d018::/32), so every query was very likely crossing the Atlantic.
That asymmetry is the whole argument for co-location: a page load is ONE
hop from the reader to Vercel, but MANY hops from Vercel to Postgres. Move
the functions next to the database and you remove the multiplied cost;
move them next to the reader and you pay it on every query instead.
VERIFY THIS VALUE. Supabase Dashboard -> Project Settings -> General shows
the region. Map it to the nearest Vercel region and set it here:
fra1 is set as the EU default. If the project turns out to be in Ireland
this is still far better than the unpinned US East it replaces — a ~20 ms
intra-EU hop instead of a transatlantic one.
